abstract: The 114th International Labour Conference adopted Convention C193 on Decent Work in the Platform Economy on June 12, 2026 — the first legally binding international treaty regulating digital platform work. The Convention extends core labor rights, occupational safety/health, adequate remuneration, data protection, and algorithmic decision-review to more than 150 million platform workers globally.
keyFindings: First-ever binding international treaty on platform work (Convention C193, 2026)
Extends freedom of association, collective bargaining, protection from discrimination/forced labor/child labor
Includes algorithmic decision-review mechanisms — first international standard requiring transparency in platform algorithms
Adopted at 114th ILC in Geneva; 5,700+ delegates from 187 Member States
methodology: Standard ILO instrument-adoption process involving tripartite consultations (governments, employers, workers) over multiple ILC sessions before the final adopting vote.
qualifiers: Conventions bind ILO Member States only upon national ratification; enforcement depends on domestic implementation which typically takes years to unfold. Coverage scope in practice will depend on how each country defines 'platform worker'.
